answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement, company-published) describing a new AI cloud partnership model, with Sharon AI CEO quote and Firmus campus figures supplied by NVIDIA.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says its new model lets AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers through a revenue-sharing and credit-support model, and that NVIDIA would earn both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity.
findings.use: Supports a reading that NVIDIA has publicly announced a commercial model combining product sales with a share of partner cloud revenue on supported capacity, which may make NVIDIA's revenue more usage-linked than a pure hardware sale.
findings.grounds: This is NVIDIA's own description of its announced model, so it reliably establishes the model's stated structure and that NVIDIA intends to earn both product and cloud-share revenue. It does not disclose the revenue-share percentage, the scope of supported capacity, pricing, or any dollar amount, and it is not a report of realized revenue. The uncertainty that matters is how large and how durable the cloud-share stream will be, which NVIDIA has not quantified.
findings.next_check: Look for NVIDIA's annual or quarterly filings that describe this program, the revenue recognition treatment of cloud-share income, and any disclosed revenue or deferred revenue tied to it.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says the model uses credit support for AI clouds, but the article gives no amount, term, counterparty limits, or conditions for that support.
findings.use: Flags a possible contingent financial exposure for NVIDIA created by credit support to partner AI clouds that needs investigation; it does not establish that NVIDIA has guaranteed any specific payment.
findings.grounds: The phrase credit-support model appears in NVIDIA's own announcement, so the existence of some credit-support arrangement is company-stated. The article does not say who provides the support, for which partners, how large it is, or whether it is guaranteed, capped, or drawn. An analyst can reasonably infer that credit support implies NVIDIA could bear credit risk on partner obligations, but that premise is an inference, not a stated fact. The relationship needed for a firm exposure conclusion is unresolved.
findings.next_check: Check NVIDIA's filings for guarantees, backstops, indemnities, purchase commitments, or other off-balance-sheet credit support tied to AI cloud partners, including amounts, maturities, and whether any have been drawn.

findings.claim: Firmus is building a DSX AI factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, which NVIDIA says is expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.
findings.use: Suggests that one partner's planned buildout could imply very large future NVIDIA GPU demand if the campus is built on the stated schedule and scale.
findings.grounds: The figures are forward-looking, stated as expected and up to, and appear in NVIDIA's own release rather than in Firmus filings or an independent project report. NVIDIA is well placed to know its planned GPU counts for a partner campus, but it is not an independent observer of the campus's build progress or financing. The main uncertainty is whether the campus reaches the stated megawatt and GPU levels, on what timeline, and how many of those GPUs will be NVIDIA-purchased versus other hardware.
findings.next_check: Look for Firmus disclosures on construction progress, power contracts, financing closes, and the timing and volume of GPU purchases for the Batam campus.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says the initiative is already taking shape, with AI cloud companies building DSX AI factories to serve customers across regions, and Sharon AI's CEO calls the collaboration a pivotal moment for its sovereign, large-scale AI compute mission.
findings.use: Supports only the narrower view that several AI cloud partners are publicly associated with DSX AI factory plans, which is a lead on partner activity rather than evidence of volume or orders.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA is describing its own partner program, and the Sharon AI CEO quote is a partner's statement of intent and enthusiasm. Neither identifies the number of factories, their capacity, their start dates, or any purchase commitment from NVIDIA. The uncertainty that matters is whether these are committed builds with NVIDIA hardware orders or aspirational partnership announcements.
findings.next_check: Check whether Sharon AI and other named AI cloud partners disclose DSX factory capacity, NVIDIA purchase agreements, or deployment timing in their own filings or announcements.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says AI natives such as Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI show where compute demand is headed, and that they need immediate access to AI cloud capacity for training, post-training, fine-tuning and agentic inference.
findings.use: Suggests the model is aimed at a demand segment NVIDIA considers high-growth, but the named companies are not shown to be buyers of the partner clouds or of NVIDIA infrastructure.
findings.grounds: This is NVIDIA's characterization of market demand, so it reflects NVIDIA's view and is not independent evidence of purchases. The named companies appear as examples of the segment rather than as stated customers in this program. The uncertainty is whether these companies actually buy capacity through the model and at what scale.
findings.next_check: Look for disclosed customer relationships between the named AI native companies and AI cloud partners, and for any reported spending on NVIDIA-based capacity by those companies.
